what: Annual fair at Kenduli, birthplace of the Vishnuvite poet Jaideva, on last day of Magh, attended by over 50,000; Vaishnav gathering.
quote: An annual fair in his honour is held in the village on the last day of the Hindu month of Madgh (the commencement of February), and is attended by upwards of*fifty thousand persons.

what: Vaishnavottar: rent-free lands for Vaishnavs/disciples of Chaitanya; also Fakirans lands for Muslim fakirs.
quote: (5) Vaishnavottar , lands bestowed rent-free upon Vaishnavs or disciples of Chaitanya. They are hereditary and transferable.

what: Fakirana: lands allotted for the maintenance of an establishment for food and shelter for fakirs (Muslim hermits).
quote: (7) Fadirdn; lands allotted for the maintenance of an establishment for providing food and shelter for fakirs or wandering Musalmdn hermits.

what: Vaishnavs described as a caste/sect with Gosain gurus cross-referenced; no Dasnami material in the Bardwan, Bankura or Birbhum accounts.
quote: (29) Vaishnav; not, properly speaking, a caste, but a class of Hindus professing to be followers of Chaitanya
